newsitem.title: USA: "Men in Black," "Contact" sparkle at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Men in Black," "Contact" sparkle at U.S. box office.

text.p: Science fiction movies held sway at the weekend box office as "Men in Black" retained the top spot, and "Contact," starring Jodie Foster, opened in second, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
"Men in Black," an alien invasion spoof starring Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones, earned about $30.5 million for the three-day Friday-to-Sunday period, bringing its gross to date to $140 million.

A spokesman for Columbia Pictures, which released the film July 2, said the studio expected it to end up in the mid-$200 million area, making it one of the few undisputed summer blockbusters. Columbia is owned by Sony Corp.

"Contact," which marks Foster's first theatrical release since 1994's "Nell," earned about $20.6 million. The actress plays a scientist who is convinced that we are not alone in the universe. Matthew McConaughey plays her love interest. The movie was directed by Robert Zemeckis, and is based on an outline for a screenplay by late astronomer Carl Sagan. "It's a superb number,,"

said Barry Reardon, president of domestic theatrical distribution at Warner Bros., noting that it played on just 1,923 screens, the smallest number in the top five. By contrast, "Men in Black" played on 3,020 screens and fifth-placed "Hercules" on 2,930.

Reardon also noted that the film's 141-minute running time restricted it to four screenings daily. On the other hand, he said its prospects were helped by the publicity surrounding the Mars Pathfinder, now renamed the Sagan Memorial Station. Warner Bros. is owned by Time Warner Inc..

"Face/Off," released by Viacom Inc. -owned Paramount Pictures, slipped a notch to third in its third weekend with $12.3 million. It was followed by Sony's "My Best Friend's Wedding" with $8.4 million, and Walt Disney Co.'s "Hercules" with $8.2 million.
